title: 단어 첫소리 ㄷ·ㅌ·ㄸ: 소리 구별과 읽기
summary: Practice distinguishing and reading the word-initial Korean consonants ㄷ (plain), ㅌ (aspirated), and ㄸ (tense). Helpful English sound references are provided so beginners can connect the sounds and read simple words accurately.
objective: Learners will identify and pronounce ㄷ (plain), ㅌ (aspirated), and ㄸ (tense) in word-initial position, link them to clear English cues (ㄷ = light t between d and t, ㅌ ≈ t in “top”, ㄸ ≈ t in “stop” but tighter), and correctly read simple words containing these initials.
exercises: 각 단어의 첫 자음(초성)을 쓰세요. Write the first consonant of each word: 두부 / 토끼 / 또
ㄸ(된소리)로 시작하는 말을 고르세요. Choose the word that starts with ㄸ (tense): 돈 / 토마토 / 떡
첫소리가 같은 두 단어를 고르세요. Choose the two words that start with the same sound: 달 / 두부 / 딸
ㅌ(거센소리)로 시작하는 말을 고르세요. Choose the word that starts with ㅌ (aspirated): 달 / 타다 / 딸
로마자 표기를 보고, 첫 자음(초성)만 한글로 쓰세요. Look at the romanization and write only the first consonant in Hangul: tteok

letters.sound: plain (lax) t, a light puff of air (lighter than ㅌ), lower pitch
letters.as: between English d and t, softer than t in “top”

letters.sound: aspirated t, strong puff of air

letters.as: close to t in “stop” (no puff), but tighter
